note: The corpus counts the noun under the rootless key m.bt.aa. The root-key spelling מימ has only a cross-reference. The key a.aj.ab belongs to the place-name element Abel in avel, although a spelling match returns it for water. The construct is מֵי and the suffixed forms also retain the stem with m, as in מֵימָיו.
summary: Water sustains the tree growing beside streams and satisfies those who thirst. The same word names the waters of a sea or flood. In Psalm 18 rescue from a powerful enemy is pictured as being drawn out of deep waters.

senses.definition: Water relieves thirst and sustains plants. Abraham offers water for washing feet, and the tree planted beside channels of water keeps its leaf and bears fruit.
senses.gloss: water to drink, wash with or sustain growth

senses.definition: The waters gathered together are called seas. The same noun names floodwaters covering the land and the waters of a river through which people pass.

evidence.note: In בֵּין מַיִם לָמָיִם the same noun names the waters on either side of the expanse.
Verse 20 measures the rise of הַמָּיִם in cubits and says the mountains were covered.
The second הַמַּיִם names the waters above the expanse.
God commands the creatures to multiply and fill the waters in the seas.
The waters increase and lift the ark above the ground, then cover the mountains.
The floodwaters prevailed over the land for 150 days.
The floodwaters subside when God sends a wind over the earth.
The waters recede from over the land and diminish.
As the floodwaters recede, the mountaintops become visible.

senses.gloss: a body or flow of water

senses.definition: The singer describes being drawn from great waters, then names the strong enemy from whom he was rescued. Elsewhere waters reaching the neck picture danger closing in.
Water spilled on the ground cannot be gathered back. The psalmist uses pouring water as an image of strength ebbing from his body.
senses.gloss: water poured out, of spent strength or lost life

senses.definition: Jesus asks the Samaritan woman for a drink at the well. Later he pours water into a basin to wash his disciples’ feet.
senses.gloss: water in which a person is washed or drinks

senses.definition: John baptizes with water, and Philip and the Ethiopian go down into the water together for baptism and come up out of it.
senses.gloss: water in which a person is baptized

senses.definition: Jesus promises water that becomes a spring in the one who receives it. John explains the promise of rivers of living water by reference to the spirit.
senses.gloss: living water given to the thirsty
